comment: Release conditions for every exact-pinned version in package.json (dependencies, devDependencies and overrides),
plus any override added to clear an npm audit advisory. An exact pin is invisible to update-npm-deps.ps1 - that
script upgrades caret ranges and skips exact versions - so nothing would ever remind you a pin is stale. This file
is what makes that check happen: on every run the script executes each `check` and compares its trimmed stdout to
`expect`. Equal means the pin is still required; different means the condition that justified the pin has changed
and the pin should be re-examined. `check: null` means no mechanical test exists - it is reported for manual review
on every run instead of going quiet. Every exact pin must have an entry here, and every entry must name a package
that is actually present in the declared section; the script reports either mismatch.

@codemirror/state.why: Obsidian provides @codemirror/state at runtime and never bundles a second copy, so the plugin compiles against the exact version Obsidian ships. The obsidian package declares that version as an EXACT peer, and @mnaoumov/obsidian-lib declares it as a caret floor, so a pin below it breaks obsidian-lib's peer and a pin above it types the Live Preview watcher against an API Obsidian does not carry. The `$@codemirror/state` override collapses every consumer onto this one copy.
@codemirror/state.manualCheck: The check reads the exact peer the installed obsidian package declares. When an obsidian bump moves it, move this pin to the same version and update `expect`.

@puppeteer/browsers.why: Clears GHSA-jmr9-qjv8-65gv (extract-zip unvalidated symlink path traversal, 8 high advisories) and nothing else. extract-zip is vulnerable at every published version, so there is no patched version to override it to, and the direct dependency cannot be bumped either: obsidian-integration-testing is already latest and pins webdriverio, and even the newest webdriverio still reaches extract-zip through @wdio/utils -> @puppeteer/browsers ^2.x. @puppeteer/browsers@3 replaced extract-zip with modern-tar, so forcing 3.x on @wdio/utils - the only consumer left on 2.x - removes the subtree entirely. It also dedupes: puppeteer-core already brings 3.2.0 into this tree, so the override collapses two copies into one rather than adding anything. The major bump is safe because @wdio/utils imports only install, canDownload, resolveBuildId, detectBrowserPlatform, Browser, ChromeReleaseChannel, computeExecutablePath and the InstallOptions type, all still exported by 3.x with compatible signatures, and both packages are ESM-only. NEVER take the `npm audit fix --force` remedy here: it downgrades obsidian-integration-testing from 10.x to 1.1.2.
@puppeteer/browsers.manualCheck: The check reads @wdio/utils's own declared range, not a version, because that range is what makes the override necessary. When it moves to ^3 or later, @wdio/utils no longer pulls extract-zip on its own and this override can be deleted along with this entry. A `require('@wdio/utils/package.json')` check would not work - its exports map does not expose package.json - hence the readFileSync form, which resolves relative to the package root the sweep runs from.

deepmerge-ts.why: Clears GHSA-ggr8-5vv4-36mx (deepmerge-ts stack exhaustion when merging recursive object graphs), patched in 8.0.0. Reached only transitively, through webdriverio -> @wdio/config / @wdio/utils / webdriver, and no direct bump gets there: every wdio package still declares deepmerge-ts@^7.0.3, the newest release included. NEVER take the `npm audit fix --force` remedy: it downgrades obsidian-integration-testing from 10.x to 1.1.2. The forced major is safe for these consumers. 8.0.0 breaks by renaming the mergeInfo system and aligning the customization shorthand, and a scan of the whole installed tree found only two bindings in use, `deepmerge` and `deepmergeCustom`. Both `deepmergeCustom` shapes present were run against 7.1.6 and 8.0.1 and produce identical output: @wdio/config's `mergeArrays` handler, which reads `meta.key` and returns `utils.actions.defaultMerge`, and webdriver's `deepmergeCustom({ mergeArrays: false })`.
deepmerge-ts.manualCheck: The check reads the range @wdio/utils declares, not a version, because that range is what forces the override. When it moves to ^8 or later the override and this entry can both go. Before lifting it, re-run the deepmergeCustom probe rather than trusting the range alone: @wdio/config passes a handler that reads `meta.key`, and that is precisely the API 8.0.0 renamed, so a regression there would be silent rather than a crash.

katex.why: Clears the KaTeX prototype-pollution trust-bypass advisory (vulnerable >=0.11.0 <0.18.2), patched in 0.18.2. Reached only transitively, through markdownlint -> micromark-extension-math, which declares katex ^0.16.0 at its latest release, so no direct bump gets there. The forced 0.x minors (0.16 to 0.19) are safe because the code that calls katex is never loaded: markdownlint imports only the `math` syntax extension, and katex is used only by micromark-extension-math's `mathHtml` HTML compiler, which nothing in the tree imports. NEVER take the `npm audit fix --force` remedy here: it fixes by downgrading the dev toolkits.
katex.manualCheck: The check reads the range micromark-extension-math declares, because that range is what makes the override necessary. When it admits 0.18.2 or later, the override and this entry can both go.

moment.why: Clears GHSA-4p3w-j4w9-5jqw (moment path traversal via a crafted non-string locale name), patched in 2.31.0. The obsidian 1.14.4 this repo develops against already resolves 2.31.0, but the obsidian 1.12.3 that eslint-plugin-obsidianmd pins EXACTLY declares moment 2.29.4 exactly, and obsidian-test-mocks resolved onto that same copy, so the tree carried the vulnerable one beside the patched one. eslint-plugin-obsidianmd 0.4.2 is the latest release, so no direct bump gets there. The override collapses both onto the version Obsidian itself ships; 2.29 to 2.31 is a minor with no API removals, and the unit suites run obsidian-test-mocks' moment against it. NEVER take the `npm audit fix --force` remedy here: it downgrades @mnaoumov/obsidian-dev-toolkit to 1.0.0.
moment.manualCheck: The check reads the exact moment the obsidian copy under eslint-plugin-obsidianmd declares. When eslint-plugin-obsidianmd moves to an obsidian that declares 2.31.0 or later, that path stops existing or the value changes, and the override and this entry can both go.

re2js.why: Clears GHSA-gg6h-894w-4m9c (RE2JS quadratic-time denial of service in lookbehind matching, >=2.2.0 <2.8.7). Reached only through markdownlint, whose newest release 0.42.0 pins re2js at the exact 2.8.6, and markdownlint-cli2 0.24.0 pins that markdownlint exactly in turn, so no bump reaches the fix. 2.9.1 is the version markdownlint itself moved to upstream, so the forced minor is the one it is tested against. NEVER take the `npm audit fix --force` remedy: it downgrades the toolkit packages.
re2js.manualCheck: The check reads the exact re2js pin of the installed markdownlint, which moves only when a markdownlint-cli2 release pins a newer markdownlint. When it reads 2.8.7 or later, drop the override and this entry and re-run `npm audit`.
